summary: Documentation is well-structured and accurately describes a non-standard project (a methodology framework, not an app). All four core files exist and are filled. Two major findings: architecture.md contains a structural diagram as a fenced code block, and deployment.md contains two bash install commands as fenced code blocks — both violate the no-code-in-docs principle.

findings.description: Directory tree is rendered as a fenced code block (lines 24-53). This is a structural diagram, not code, but it still uses a code block and will drift as the repo evolves.
findings.recommendation: Replace the code block with a prose description of the top-level directories and their roles, or convert to a markdown table. Example: '`{skill-name}/SKILL.md` — skill instructions; `shared/` — scripts and templates; `work/` — per-feature working directories (gitignored or per-feature commit).' The directory names themselves can stay as inline code spans.

findings.description: Two fenced bash blocks contain git clone and git pull commands (lines 22-25 and 28-30). These are exact shell commands embedded in documentation.
findings.recommendation: Convert to prose with inline code for the repo URL and target path. Example: 'Clone `https://github.com/stepanenkoviktor0110-boop/ai-dev-methodology` into `~/.claude/skills/`. Update via `git pull origin master` from that directory.' One-liner commands fit cleanly as inline code; multi-step sequences belong in a runbook file if needed.

findings.description: The Codex path-substitution rule (`.claude/` → `.agents/`, `Agent` tool → `spawn_agent`/`wait_agent`/`close_agent`) is stated in full in patterns.md and is also described in architecture.md under 'Platform Differences: Claude vs Codex' (table + prose). The technical facts appear in both files.
findings.recommendation: Keep the comparison table in architecture.md as the single source of platform differences. In patterns.md, replace the full rule with a cross-reference: 'See architecture.md — Platform Differences for path and API substitutions.'
